title: Reconstruct ResNet
summary: Recover the residual-learning argument, identity shortcut, and stage design, then implement the smallest working residual block.

parts.title: The degradation problem
parts.prompt: Why can a deeper plain network have higher training error even though it could represent the shallower solution?
parts.answer: In principle the added layers could learn identity mappings, but optimization does not reliably find them. The degradation result showed an optimization problem, not ordinary overfitting.
hints: Compare training error, not only validation error.
What function should extra layers learn to preserve the old model?

parts.title: Learn the residual
parts.prompt: Why parameterize F(x)=H(x)-x and output F(x)+x instead of learning H(x) directly?
parts.answer: The shortcut makes identity easy: drive residual weights toward zero. Gradients also have a direct additive path through the block, which makes very deep networks easier to optimize.
hints: Follow the gradient through the addition.

parts.title: Match dimensions safely
parts.prompt: When can the shortcut be an identity, and what must happen when feature dimensions or resolution change?
parts.answer: Identity shortcuts require matching shapes. At stage transitions, a projection shortcut or padding/downsampling aligns dimensions before addition.
hints: Stage boundaries commonly change channels and resolution.

parts.title: Implement ReLU
parts.prompt: Implement the elementwise ReLU used after residual additions.

parts.title: Implement a residual block
parts.prompt: Implement two linear transforms with an intermediate ReLU, add the identity shortcut, and apply a final ReLU.
